results.title: Le Pen denies receiving leaked information from French interior ministry official
results.content: French far-right leader Marine Le Pen on Sunday said she did not receive, nor ask for, confidential information on an investigation into her party from a senior interior ministry official. She however could not say if other party members had benefited from the leaks. Hugues Moutouh, the civil servant under suspicion, has denied the allegations and asked to be relieved of his duties pending a probe.

results.title: Ligue 1: PSG extend winning run at Nice (3-2) but lose Désiré Doué to injury
results.content: A bittersweet victory for PSG at Nice on Saturday evening. The Parisians strengthened their grip on top spot in Ligue 1, but lost Désiré Doué for several months after the forward suffered a serious knee injury.

results.title: West Bank attacks: Opposition leader Eisenkot decries "Jewish terrorism"
results.content: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were set on fire in three villages in the occupied West Bank. Israeli soldiers were deployed to the area following the attacks, which local residents said were carried out by Israeli settlers. Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, condemned the acts on X, describing them as “Jewish terrorism”. Antonia Kerrigan reports.

results.title: Russian strike kills 2 in Kyiv
results.content: A Russian attack struck an apartment building in the village of Dymer, just north of Kyiv, on Sunday, killing at least two people and wounding four others. The morning strike destroyed a five-storey building, while rescuers evacuated nine people, including a child. At least 11 others are believed to remain trapped under the rubble.

results.title: The week in pictures: Xi hosts Trump and Putin, COP31 and new French protests
results.content: From the unprecedented Shenzhen summit in China that saw President Xi Jinping host his US and Russian counterparts, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, to tough talks at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey and another week of French protests over the cost of living, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.

results.title: "It can take years": Why the AI Riemann proof is far from settled
results.content: AI claimed another major scalp in maths on Friday, as Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published what he says is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a Millennium Prize Problem, in 17 million lines of code that no human has read in full. Physicist Tony Padilla tells Tech 24 that verification could take years, and that Alpöge should share how he got there.

results.title: Israel investigates West Bank fires
results.content: Israeli authorities have opened an investigation after Palestinian vehicles and properties were vandalised and set on fire in four villages in the occupied West Bank, in attacks local activists say were carried out by Israeli settlers. Around eight vehicles were reportedly torched and racist slogans sprayed on walls, prompting Israeli soldiers and police to deploy to the area. The attacks come amid a surge in settler violence since the outbreak of the Gaza war in October 2023, with more than 1,100 Palestinians killed by Israeli soldiers or settlers in the West Bank since then, according to an AFP tally. They also follow recent sanctions announced by the UK and Australia against eight Israeli companies involved in settlement activity. France 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky shares further details from Jerusalem.

results.title: 🔴 COP31 ends without deal as EU rejects text for omitting mention of fossil fuels
Indonesia factory hit by deadly blaze: Three killed and 36 missing
results.content: At least three people have been killed and dozens are missing after a fire broke out at a factory in Indonesia producing sweets and snack products. Fifteen people were rescued alive from the plant, while firefighters were still battling flames in several parts of the facility more than 12 hours after the blaze began. The cause of the fire remains unknown, but survivors said it started in a cooling unit on the third floor.

results.title: Former Italian police chief found dead
results.content: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has expressed shock following the death of a former national police chief, whose body was found on Saturday. He had been under investigation over an alleged cover-up in an inquiry into a bombing linked to organised crime in Sicily. Jennie Shin reports.

results.title: Princess of Wales opens up about cancer
results.content: A new documentary titled Heal follows Britain’s Princess Catherine as she navigates life since her cancer diagnosis in 2024. The film tracks the 44-year-old as she attempts to climb the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales within 24 hours. In the trailer, she reflects on healing as a journey. Ophelie Jacobson reports.

results.title: South Korea: AI cheating sparks exam security chaos
results.content: South Korea’s education minister resigned on Sunday following a major cheating scandal that erupted just ahead of the country’s university entrance exams. The controversy centred on the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam, who admitted to using a miniature camera and smartphone to secure a near-perfect result. Jack Pownall reports.

results.title: Europe sees new protests over rising costs, inequality and public services
results.content: Sunday marks the third consecutive day of protests across Europe, following large demonstrations on Friday and smaller rallies on Saturday, from Portugal to France. The protests have largely focused on the rising cost of living and access to affordable housing. In France, demonstrations have now taken place for six weekends in a row. Ophelie Jacobson reports.

results.title: English village votes to "leave UK"
results.content: Residents of the small English village of Barnham voted on Saturday in a symbolic referendum to leave the UK, in protest against government plans to house 931 asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base – more than the village’s own population of 584. The vote follows a similar protest in another village in September, highlighting growing tensions over immigration across the country. Earlier this week, the leader of a far-right anti-immigration group was jailed, but supporters have vowed to keep the movement alive. Jack Pownall reports.

results.title: NATO faces sovereignty dilemma as militaries rely on private tech, AI
results.content: NATO officials and defence experts gathered at the NATO Edge conference in Turkey this week to discuss how militaries can harness artificial intelligence and high tech without compromising control over sensitive data and defence capabilities.

results.title: Live: Ukrainian rescuers search for survivors in rubble after Russian attack
results.content: Ukrainian rescue teams on Sunday searched for survivors in the rubble of a collapsed residential building in Dymer, in the Kyiv region, after a Russian drone strike, which killed two people and wounded four others. Meanwhile, Finland warned the war was "spilling over" after a drone set fire to a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea Saturday. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

results.title: South Korean education minister resigns over AI-driven exam cheating scandal
results.content: South Korea Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned Sunday over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that erupted days before the high-stakes Suneung university entrance exam. The Suneung concluded "without any major incidents" last week, Choi said, but he admitted to a failure to "prepare adequately in advance".

results.title: Bahrain accuses Iran of striking industrial site as tankers hit in Hormuz
results.content: Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial site on Saturday evening, as two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran reported shooting down a US drone amid stalled efforts to end the war.

results.title: EU-Indonesia agreement sees the light after ten years of negotiations
results.content: The European Union and Indonesia have signed a major trade deal, ten years after talks began.The agreement removes almost all tariffs between the EU and Southeast Asia's biggest economy: 98.5 per cent of them. For Europe, it means access to a market of 280 million people and a steadier supply of nickel for batteries. For Indonesia, easier exports of palm oil, textiles and footwear, and it arrives just before its current EU trade preferences end on the 1st of January. To discuss the deal Airlangga Hartarto, Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs in Indonesia joined us on the programme.

results.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for ‘marathon’ Israeli coalition talks
results.content: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has invited caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party for coalition talks, his centrist Yashar party said Saturday. The "marathon series of talks" starts Sunday, the party said, adding that the move reflected a commitment to form "the broadest possible government" after the October election failed to deliver an outright winner.

results.title: France’s sixth consecutive Saturday of protests draws lower turnout
results.content: Turnout ⁠was down ​at largely peaceful demonstrations across France on the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests ​over the cost of living, with the interior ministry putting the figure at 82,500 across the country. Organisers said 150,000 people participated in the nationwide protests, down from their 200,000 figure last week.

results.title: 'Worst Ever' COP Summit?
results.content: Is this the worst COP summit on record? With limited political leadership, no official US delegation and mounting frustration over bureaucratic delays, questions are being raised about the effectiveness of the climate negotiations. Juan Carlos Beldsoe, a former White House climate adviser under Bill Clinton, described the process as labyrinthine and ultimately dispiriting. France 24's Gavin Lee speaks with climate advocate and six-time COP delegate, Henna Hundal about what this means for the future of global climate action.

results.title: Russia attacks Zelensky's hometown, Ukraine reaffirms wish to join NATO
results.content: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.

results.title: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on Zelensky's hometown in central Ukraine
results.content: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv.
